says: The delete-value, number, text, list-of-strings and new-value dialogs have code that cancels the dialog when Escape is pressed, but it never runs: none of these dialogs lets the form see key presses typed in its controls, and none has a Cancel button. Escape therefore does not close them; they close only through their own buttons.

In the hexadecimal number box, typed text is read as an unsigned hex number. If it is too large to read as a 64-bit number, or larger than the box's maximum (4294967295 for a 32-bit DWord), the box takes the maximum. Text that is not valid hex, including text with a minus sign, leaves the value unchanged. Empty text is ignored.

Pressing the Cancel button (also labelled Close, and the dialog's cancel button) closes the setting dialog reporting OK if at least one Apply was done during this opening, and Cancel otherwise. The OK button always reports OK.

Applying with Enabled selected stores the policy as Enabled together with the value of each option control: numbers, text, tick state, the chosen dropdown entry, the list and the lines of multi-line text. Label-only elements store nothing.

When Apply or OK is pressed with Enabled selected and a dropdown option has no choice selected, nothing is stored and no message is shown: the policy's previous configuration was already removed, and the action fails with an unhandled error. A dropdown starts without a choice when the presentation names no default or the stored value matches no item, so the person must pick one first.
